Tessa / Aisha —

I reviewed the buyer redlines attached. Short version: these are elevated legal risks and an unconditional approval would need senior exec sign-off. My recommendations below.

1) Warranty: Buyer seeks to remove our warranty exclusion and add an express warranty for service availability/data handling. We can offer a limited warranty: 99.5% monthly uptime SLA for API endpoints used in the pilot with exclusions for force majeure/maintenance and a capped SLA credit mechanism. We should not accept an open-ended warranty tied to business outcomes.

2) Indemnity: We must resist an indemnity that covers regulatory fines. If customer insists, we can offer a narrowly tailored indemnity for third-party IP infringement and third-party claims resulting from Redwood's willful misconduct. We should add a required obligation for the customer to carry appropriate insurance and include an insurer-notify clause.

3) Liability cap: Moving to 2x ARR ($480k) is higher risk. Proposed compromise: increase to $350k for the pilot term, subject to the following protective measures: (a) carve-outs for gross negligence/willful misconduct, (b) combined cap across claims, (c) require purchase of cyber insurance with minimum limits. If they insist on $480k, this needs CEO signoff and a commercial offset (higher price or indemnity restrictions).

If leadership is prepared to accept these compromises, I will prepare a clean redline with language and mark the specific clauses that require exec approval. Otherwise, we should push back to customer with the alternatives above.

—Markus Klein
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
